name: Asado de Puerco (Mexican Red Chile Pork Stew) Bowls
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Pork simmered in red chile colorado sauce; source states 293 cal / 26g protein per serving over 10 servings for the stew, so plated over rice and beans it clears 550+ cal and 30g protein. Distinct from the live green chili and salsa verde pork bowls (red chile, not green). Braise scales linearly to 14 servings. | HARVEST: '4 cups Red Chile Sauce' links to a separate component recipe on the same site; its sub-ingredients are not listed on this page.
intro_html: In Chihuahua and across the border in El Paso, asado de puerco is the dish that comes out for weddings, baptisms and Christmas Eve. Pork simmered slowly in red chile sauce until the sauce clings to every piece and the meat surrenders. Traditionally you toast and blend the dried chiles yourself. Canned red enchilada sauce gets you most of the way there on a weeknight, which is why this one lands where it does on the receipt.
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Rice, 7.25 cups dry: ~$1.63. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 2 2lb bags.
Pantry seasonings (salt, ground cumin, black pepper): ~$0.24. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $16.71 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.19 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $19.48 across 14 servings, roughly $1.39 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $16.61 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $36.09. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About $2.58 a bowl (at everyday cost), and it does not eat like a budget plate. Six ingredients, one pot, and pork loin doing the work.
shop_smart: Canned enchilada sauce is the shortcut worth taking. Toasting and blending dried chiles is better, but it is also an hour and a blender. The canned sauce costs about a dollar and gets you close.
Pork loin goes on sale hard. Watch for the whole loin price and cut it down yourself. You will pay a fraction of what precut cubes or chops cost per pound.
Plain tomato sauce rounds the chile. One cheap can takes the edge off the heat and gives the sauce body. It is the least expensive ingredient in the pot and it matters.
Rice from the big bag is why this costs what it does. The carb here is close to free per serving, which leaves the budget for the meat.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the pork loin into bite-sized cubes and pat them dry, then season with salt, ground cumin and black pepper.
Sear the pork in the olive oil in a heavy pot over high heat, in batches, until the pieces are browned on at least two sides. Crowding the pan is the one mistake to avoid here.
Drop the heat, add the minced garlic, and stir for a minute until it smells sweet.
Pour in the enchilada sauce and the tomato sauce, scrape the bottom of the pot clean, and bring it to a bare simmer.
Cover and simmer gently for about 90 minutes, stirring now and then, until the pork is tender and the sauce has thickened and darkened.
Cook the rice per the package while the pork simmers, and taste the sauce for salt at the end.
portion_html: Spread the cooked rice across your 14 containers, then set the pot on your scale, subtract the empty pot weight from Step 1, divide by 14, and spoon that exact weight of pork and red chile sauce over the rice. Every bowl lands near 567 calories with 32 grams of protein.

upsell_html: Northern Mexican red chile pork for about $2.58 a bowl (at everyday cost). This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.

head.description: Cubed pork loin simmered slowly in red chile and tomato sauce, served over rice. A 14 serving asado de puerco built for very cheap meal prep.
head.keywords: asado de puerco, red chile pork, chile colorado recipe, mexican pork stew, pork rice bowls, budget meal prep
steps: Cube and season the pork loin with salt, cumin and black pepper.
Sear the pork in olive oil in batches until well browned.
Add the garlic, then pour in the enchilada sauce and tomato sauce.
Cover and simmer about 90 minutes until the pork is tender and the sauce thickens.
